title: Accounts Assistant

The Role
Reporting into the finance team, you will take responsibility for the day-to-day running of the purchase ledger, ensuring invoices, payments and expenses are processed accurately and efficiently.
Key responsibilities will include:
- Processing purchase invoices and credit notes, ensuring accurate coding and posting to the accounting system.
- Maintaining supplier accounts and ensuring records are accurate and up to date.
- Preparing and processing supplier payment runs in line with agreed payment terms.
- Reconciling supplier statements and investigating any discrepancies.

The successful candidate will have previous experience working in an Accounts Payable or Purchase Ledger role and will be confident managing a busy workload while maintaining a high level of accuracy.
You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in an Accounts Payable / Purchase Ledger position.
- Good knowledge of invoice processing, supplier reconciliations and payment runs.

- Confident communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with suppliers and colleagues.

In addition to hybrid working, the business offers an excellent range of benefits.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
BOOKKEEPER

ABOUT US

Flux Pumps International (UK) Ltd

Flux Pumps UK is a leading distributor of industrial pumps for emptying drums, containers and tanks. We are a wholly owned subsidiary of our parent company Flux-Gereate GmbH. Our Corporate headquarters and manufacturing facility is based near Stuttgart, in Germany.

FLUX has been manufacturing world leading pumps since 1950. Our products are designed for the longest service life in the toughest applications. We supply pumps and flow meters for almost any fluid water, oils, solvents, flammable liquids, food and pharmaceutical products. Our extensive range of products is suitable for transfer, emptying, mixing, filling and metering. Key industries served include manufacturing, surface finishing, paints, petrochemicals, food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and water treatment.

The Flux range is centred on the class-leading F400 series barrel & IBC pumps. We also manufacture the CombiFlux battery operated container pump - the World's first battery powered chemical pump for industrial use. Other products include one-touch dispensing systems, hygienic pumps and Viscopower pumps for handling high viscosity fluids eg. tomato paste or cosmetic cream.

Flux UK is a dynamic, sales focussed business - we do our utmost to provide industry leading customer service. As a result, our business has grown impressively over the past 10 years. Please check the customer feedback on our website.

The Role

Due to an internal promotion, we have an exciting opportunity for a Bookkeeper to join our small, friendly team. The role is an office-based position working alongside our operations team and reporting to the UK Director. The role requires at least 5 years book-keeping experience (experience with Sage accounting software is essential) and ideally basic knowledge of UK GAAP.

Remote working is not permitted for this role.

Responsibilities

Sales Ledger
- Creating sales invoices from shipping documents and e-mailing to customers

Purchase Ledger
- Processing all purchase invoices
- Matching stock receipts to purchase invoices for stock items
- Compiling a monthly suppliers payment list

Banking
- Check bank receipts and payments daily

Fixed Asset Register
- Maintaining the register by adding and disposing of records as necessary

Month End Journal Postings
- Making supplementary journal postings each month to reconcile accounts
- Running a monthly trial balance

Office Administration
- Assist with annual stock-take
- Any other ad hoc duties that may be required

Working Hours

9 30 Mon-Thurs with 30 minutes for lunch (24 hours per week). Alternative working patterns may be considered.

Working Environment

The role is based at our Verwood office.

Training

The candidate will receive training on our ProAlpha ERP system.

Benefits

Competitive salary.

The Company operates a contributory pension scheme (6% company contribution).

22 days holiday (increasing by 1 extra day with every 2 years service, to a maximum of 25 days).

To apply

Please e-mail CV and covering letter explaining your suitability for the role.

Start date: ASAP

Job Type: Part-time

Pay: up to £15.50 per hour (depending on experience)

Benefits:
- Company pension
- Free on-site parking

Schedule:
- Part-time Monday to Thursday

Education/ Qualifications / Experience required:
- Minimum 5 years experience in Bookkeeping is essential
- Experience with Sage accounting software is essential
- Ideally AAT Level 2 Certificate in Bookkeeping, or equivalent
- A Levels or equivalent
- GCSE s

Licence / Certification:
- Driving Licence beneficial

Work authorisation:
- United Kingdom (essential)

Work Location: In person

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Chalk Hill Group are working with a growing financial services business, in Poole, to recruit a Payroll Administrator to join their team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced payroll professional who enjoys managing their own client portfolio, building strong relationships and ensuring payrolls are processed accurately and on time.

The Role
- Manage a portfolio of approximately 30-50 payrolls per month, from input and imports through to checking and processing.
- Calculate statutory payments, including maternity, sick and holiday pay.
- Handle payroll queries, investigate discrepancies and ensure accurate, timely processing.
- Build strong relationships with clients, acting as a key point of contact for payroll-related queries.
- Manage competing deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
- Work with Excel spreadsheets, including data manipulation and importing payroll information.

About You
- Previous hands-on payroll experience, ideally managing your own client portfolio.
- Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach to your work.
- Highly organised, with the ability to manage multiple payroll deadlines.
- Confident communicating directly with clients and building lasting relationships.
- Good Excel skills, particularly spreadsheet manipulation and data imports.
- Experience with Xero knowledge also beneficial.

Salary & Benefits
- Salary of up to £30,000, depending on experience.
- Hybrid working available following probation: office-based Tuesday to Thursday, with the option to work from home on Mondays and Fridays.
- Five days per week in the office during the probationary period.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Are you an experienced payroll professional who enjoys working closely with clients and taking ownership of your work?

We're looking for a Payroll Administrator to join a friendly and collaborative payroll team, delivering accurate, reliable and responsive payroll services to a diverse portfolio of businesses.

This is a client-facing role where you'll have the opportunity to build strong relationships, manage your own portfolio and play an important part in ensuring payrolls are processed accurately and on time.

The Role

As a Payroll Administrator, you'll take responsibility for a portfolio of clients, working closely with them to deliver a high-quality payroll service while supporting the wider team.

What you'll be doing
- Processing a variety of client payrolls as part of a collaborative payroll team
- Acting as the primary point of contact for an allocated portfolio of clients
- Managing client payrolls from start to finish, ensuring accuracy and compliance
- Supporting the onboarding of new clients and payrolls, ensuring data is complete and accurate
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes, increase efficiency and enhance the client experience
- Building and maintaining strong, professional client relationships
- Responding to payroll queries accurately, professionally and within agreed timescales
- Keeping up to date with changes in payroll legislation and ensuring these are correctly applied
- Liaising with HMRC regarding employer payments and payroll-related matters
- Ensuring payroll deadlines are consistently met
- Working collaboratively with colleagues and providing support where required

About You

You'll be an organised and detail-focused payroll professional who takes pride in delivering an accurate and dependable service.

You'll ideally have:
- Strong knowledge and practical experience of UK payroll legislation
- Experience managing a portfolio of clients or multiple payrolls
- A proven track record of delivering excellent client service
- Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to your work
- Confident written and verbal communication skills
- The ability to build positive working relationships with a wide range of clients
- The ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a wider team
- Excellent organisation and time-management skills, with the ability to work to strict deadlines
- Good numerical and analytical skills
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Excel, Word and Outlook
- A professional, courteous and solutions-focused approach

What's on Offer?

You'll join an organisation that values its people and provides a supportive environment in which to develop your career.

Alongside a competitive salary, you'll have access to a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your financial, physical and mental wellbeing.

Financial wellbeing
- Employer-supported pension scheme
- Group life assurance
- Income protection
- Health cash plan, including support for eligible dependants

Mental wellbeing
- Confidential counselling and emotional support
- Virtual GP and second-opinion services
- Access to trained Mental Health First Aiders
- A range of resources to support your overall wellbeing

Physical wellbeing
- Cycle to work scheme
- Access to discounted gym, pool and fitness memberships
- Digital health and wellbeing resources
- Support and resources around menopause and women's health

Additional benefits
- Family-friendly benefits and enhanced family leave
- The opportunity to purchase additional annual leave
- Paid volunteering day each year
- Electric vehicle lease scheme, subject to eligibility
- Recognition of key career and family milestones
- Regular expert-led wellbeing webinars
- Access to charitable support for colleagues experiencing financial hardship

Why Join?

This is an excellent opportunity to join an established and forward-thinking professional services organisation where people are encouraged to develop, collaborate and make a genuine contribution.

You'll work alongside experienced payroll professionals, supporting a varied client base and gaining exposure to a broad range of payroll requirements.

The organisation offers a flexible approach to hybrid working, alongside a strong focus on learning, development, wellbeing and creating an inclusive working environment where people can be themselves.

If you're an experienced payroll professional looking for a role where client relationships, technical expertise and quality service are equally important, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more.

title: Payroll Assistant

title: Purchase Ledger Administrator
description:
REED Accountancy are actively recruiting a TEMP (potential to go permanent) Purchase Ledger Administrator for an Education Establishment based near Yeovil, Dorset. Joining a finance team and reporting into the Assistant Finance Director, you will have experience processing volume invoices, supplier payments and reconciliations accurately and efficiently.

Purchase Ledger Administrator
- Hours: 37.5 hours per week (typically 8.30am-5.00pm Monday-Friday).
- Reporting to: Assistant Directors of Finance.
- Duration - 6 months (potential to extend)
- Start Date:ASAP (After Enhanced DBS and safeguarding checks completed)
- Pay rate - £14.50 PAYE / £18.50 Umbrella

Duties:
- Processing supplier invoices and ensuring correct authorisation and coding.
- Managing BACS payment runs and occasional cheque payments.
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving queries.
- Setting up and maintaining supplier accounts.
- Administering charity accounts and ensuring donations are correctly allocated.
- Processing Foundation transactions, bank reconciliations and gift aid controls.
- Maintaining financial records and filing systems.
- Posting journals and supporting wider finance team activities.
- Assisting with departmental purchasing and online orders.

Requirements
- Previous experience within a finance or accounts environment, specifically processing purchase invoices in volume
- Holds an AAT qualification (Level 2/3) / Part Qualified AAT or is qualified through experience.
- Has strong numerical accuracy and attention to detail.
- Is confident using Microsoft Office applications.

description:
Accounts Payable AssistantBridport, Dorset Temporary, initially 3 months 37.5 hours per week Office-based

Are you an experienced Accounts Payable Assistant looking for your next temporary opportunity?

We're recruiting for an Accounts Payable Assistant to join the Finance team of an established business based in Bridport. This is an initial 3-month temporary assignment, working 37.5 hours per week across five days (they would be open to considering someone only looking to work 4 days per week).

The role will be fully office-based, although there may be some flexibility around start and finish times.

The role

Working as part of the Finance team, you'll support the smooth running of the Accounts Payable function and help ensure supplier invoices and payments are processed accurately and efficiently.
- Processing a high volume of supplier invoices accurately and on time
- Matching invoices against purchase orders and supporting documentation
- Coding invoices to the appropriate nominal ledger accounts
- Reconciling supplier statements and investigating discrepancies
- Setting up and maintaining supplier accounts and records
- Supporting with the incoming phone lines and responding to supplier queries by telephone and email
- Processing employee expenses where required
- Supporting month-end processes, including Accounts Payable reconciliations
- Maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring information is correctly recorded within the finance system
- Providing general administrative support to the wider Finance team as required

What we're looking for

You'll ideally have previous experience in an Accounts Payable, Purchase Ledger or transactional finance role and be comfortable working in a busy, hands-on environment.
- Previous Accounts Payable or Purchase Ledger experience
- Good attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Confidence working with invoices, supplier statements and reconciliations
- Good numerical and data-entry skills
- Competent Excel and general Microsoft Office skills
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
- A professional and confident approach when dealing with suppliers and internal colleagues
- The ability to work independently as well as part of a wider Finance team
- A proactive approach to resolving queries and discrepancies

Key details:
- Bridport, Dorset
- Initial 3-month temporary contract
- 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday
- Fully office-based
- Potential flexibility around start and finish times
- Immediate / short-notice availability advantageous
